questions.question: Q1. What does the 'fourth dimension' refer to in 4D printing?

answers.a: The use of four different materials in one print.
answers.b: The programmed transformation of the flat structure over time when a stimulus is applied.
answers.c: The four types of 3D printers that can do this.

explanations.a: Incorrect - Material count is not the defining feature.
explanations.b: Correct - The fourth dimension is time; the structure changes shape after printing in response to an external stimulus.
explanations.c: Incorrect - The type of printer is not what defines the fourth dimension.
explanations.d: Incorrect - The number of steps is not the defining characteristic.

questions.question: Q2. Why is stiffness contrast (SC = E_panel / E_hinge) important in self-folding box design?

answers.a: It ensures the fold stays localized in the hinge rather than spreading into the rigid panels.
answers.b: It determines how fast the material cools after printing.
answers.c: It controls the color of the printed material.
answers.d: It sets the maximum temperature the box can withstand.

explanations.a: Correct - High SC keeps the bending concentrated in the soft hinge; low SC causes the fold to spread and round the corners.
explanations.b: Incorrect - Cooling rate is a printing parameter, not a design principle.
explanations.c: Incorrect - Material color is not related to stiffness contrast.
explanations.d: Incorrect - Thermal limits are a material property, not a stiffness ratio.

questions.question: Q3. The Kutzbach-Grübler mobility formula F = 3(n - 1) - 2j₁ - j₂ predicts the degrees of freedom of a mechanism. Which mobility target is ideal for a self-closing gripper?

answers.a: F = 0, because the gripper should be rigid.
answers.b: F = 1, because it needs to move in only one direction.
answers.c: F = 2, because it allows controlled opening and closing.
answers.d: F > 2, because more freedom means better gripping.

explanations.a: Incorrect - A rigid gripper cannot open or close.
explanations.b: Incorrect - F = 1 is too restrictive for control.
explanations.c: Correct - F = 2 gives exactly the controllable motion needed to open and close the gripper jaws smoothly.
explanations.d: Incorrect - F > 2 makes the gripper floppy and unpredictable.

questions.question: Q4. In forward kinematics of a hinge chain, what does the tip position depend on?

answers.a: Only the length of the first panel.
answers.b: The cumulative sum of all hinge angles and panel lengths.

explanations.a: Incorrect - All panels contribute to the tip position.
explanations.b: Correct - Forward kinematics maps hinge angles θᵢ and panel lengths to the final tip (x, y) by summing rotations.
explanations.c: Incorrect - Geometry drives kinematics, not material properties.
explanations.d: Incorrect - Environmental factors do not affect the kinematic geometry.

questions.question: Q5. What is the signature property of a Miura-ori tessellation that makes it useful for solar panels and deployable structures?

answers.a: It stores more energy than other origami patterns.
answers.b: It requires no actuation to deploy.
answers.c: It is stronger than any other folded material.
answers.d: It has a negative Poisson's ratio, so pulling it open in one direction expands it in both directions.

explanations.a: Incorrect - Energy storage is not the key feature.
explanations.b: Incorrect - Miura-ori does require controlled actuation to deploy.
explanations.c: Incorrect - Strength is not the defining property.
explanations.d: Correct - Auxetic behavior (negative Poisson's ratio) means a single actuation deploys the entire array in both directions.

questions.question: Q6. Which physical quantity determines the peak cyclic stress in a living hinge under repeated folding?

answers.a: The hinge thickness and bend radius.
answers.c: The color of the printed material.

explanations.a: Correct - Peak strain ε_max = h/(2R), and stress σ = E_eff · ε_max depend on thickness h and radius R = L/θ.
explanations.b: Incorrect - Length alone does not determine stress.
explanations.c: Incorrect - Material color is not a mechanical property.
explanations.d: Incorrect - Room temperature does not determine the stress state during use.

questions.question: Q7. What does a localisation fraction f_hinge close to 100% tell you about a self-folding box?

answers.b: The hinge is too soft and will tear immediately.
answers.c: Almost all of the rotation stays in the hinge; the panels stay nearly flat and the corners are sharp.
answers.d: The fold will take a long time to complete.

explanations.a: Incorrect - f_hinge ≈ 1 means crisp folding, not permanent locking.
explanations.b: Incorrect - High SC (which gives high f_hinge) means the hinge is appropriately soft, not failing.
explanations.c: Correct - High f_hinge means the fold is localized in the hinge, leaving panels rigid and corners sharp.
explanations.d: Incorrect - Localisation fraction does not control folding speed.

questions.question: Q8. In Sub-Calc C, why is cyclic coordinate descent (CCD) used instead of a closed-form solution?

answers.b: Closed-form solutions exist but are rarely used in practice.
answers.c: Closed-form solutions only work for two-link arms.
answers.d: A general serial hinge chain has no closed-form inverse kinematics, so iteration is necessary.

explanations.a: Incorrect - CCD is iterative, so it's not inherently faster.
explanations.b: Incorrect - Closed-form solutions do not exist for the general case.
explanations.c: Incorrect - While closed-form solutions exist for 2-link arms, this limitation is not why CCD is used here.
explanations.d: Correct - Inverse kinematics for chains longer than 2-3 links requires numerical methods like CCD.

questions.question: Q9. What safety factor is applied in Sub-Calc E to convert the theoretical cycle life N to a dependable life N_safe?

explanations.a: Incorrect - The safety factor is higher than 2.
explanations.b: Correct - A polymer safety factor of 5 gives N_safe = N/5; the hinge is considered long-lived when N_safe ≥ 1000.
explanations.c: Incorrect - The safety factor is higher than 3.
explanations.d: Incorrect - The safety factor is lower than 10.

questions.question: Q10. How does reducing the hinge thickness affect the fatigue life of a living hinge?

answers.a: It increases the fatigue life exponentially because thinner hinges have lower peak stress.
answers.b: It has no effect on fatigue life.
answers.c: It decreases the fatigue life because thinner hinges are weaker.
answers.d: It decreases the fatigue life logarithmically.

explanations.a: Correct - Since ε_max = h/(2R) and the Basquin exponent b = 0.1 is small, halving h lowers stress dramatically and moves the S-N curve far to the right, buying exponentially more cycles.
explanations.b: Incorrect - Thickness directly affects the strain and thus the stress.
explanations.c: Incorrect - While intuitive, lower stress more than compensates for reduced thickness.
explanations.d: Incorrect - The relationship is exponential, not logarithmic.
